the medium

what a reaction identifier does not carry

direction · refusal · a retrieval allocator that declines rather than guessing

kundai sachikonye · a second approach to the same problem

one identifier, two directions

E. coli AlaA carries the same Rhea master identifier as human ALT1 — and runs the reaction the other way.
E. coli AlaAhuman ALT1
participantsidenticalidentical
stoichiometryidenticalidentical
Rhea masterthe samethe same
directionone waythe other

in every representation I know of, that difference is asserted — a vocabulary term attached by a curator

the graph cannot say it

a reaction is direction-symmetric by construction — and that is a theorem, not an omission

reversal invariance

Write the reaction as a chain of steps, and reverse it. The reversal commits

  • the same total boundary
  • the same number of steps
  • the same set of committed edges

all three are sums or sets — invariant under reordering

the consequence

No predicate definable from the reaction's own structure distinguishes it from its reverse.

So direction cannot come from inside. It has to come from something the identifier does not name.

the medium

the medium as a reservoir

a species is cheap to pick out when it is scarce, expensive when it is everywhere

w(species, medium)  =  β · ( 1 + log(1 + τ / μ) )

  μ   ambient occupancy of that species in the medium
  τ   exchange rate with the surroundings
  β   the floor — the least distinguishable difference

only two properties of this are load-bearing: it is monotone in scarcity, and it is bounded below by β.

the exact functional form is a modelling choice — §7 re-runs every structural result under four unrelated weight families to check that nothing depends on the logarithm

direction, derived

medium bias: what it costs to individuate the products, minus the reactants

Δ(chain, medium)  =  Σ w(products)  −  Σ w(reactants)

reversing the chain flips the sign of Δ by construction — this is the asymmetry the chain itself could not provide

Δ > 0 means the products are scarcer than the reactants: the medium is depleted at the product end, and pulls the reaction that way.

three cases, not two

compare the bias against the floor β — exactly one holds

conditionverdict
Δ > βirreversible in the written direction
Δ < −βirreversible in the reverse direction
|Δ| ≤ βundirected in this medium — the system declines to orient it

so reversibility is a property of the pair (reaction, medium) — never of the reaction alone

and the same reaction may fall in different cases in different media — which is exactly the AlaA case, now a corollary rather than a curation decision

the same molecule as the first deck

alanine transaminase: L-alanine + 2-oxoglutarate → pyruvate + L-glutamate

glutamate held depleted

downstream demand keeps L-glutamate scarce; 2-oxoglutarate is ambient.

Δ > β → runs forward

2-oxoglutarate held depleted

the same enzyme, feeding nitrogen the other way.

Δ < −β → runs in reverse

neither organism's enzyme differs in the reaction it performs. Both are correct.

a framework that refuses

A representation earns a positive result only if some presentable object would have received a negative one. A framework with no refusals has an empty defined class: it does not classify, it merely accepts.

the medium supplies two refusals, of different kinds

refusalwhat fires it
refuse to individuatebulk solvent — a fluctuation of the medium, not a part of the system
refuse to orienta chain whose bias falls inside the floor

both are proved attainable by objects the language can construct — a refusal that never fires is not a refusal

a test that failed

the first direction sweep reported forward nine times, undirected ten times, and reverse never — an apparent refutation

the theorem was not at fault. The sweep was one-sided — and one-sided sweeps cannot reach the reverse case:

flooding a single product drives the bias to  −β·log 2

  |Δ|  →  0.693 β   <   β        the chain stays UNDIRECTED

  checked numerically at μ = 10^30:  −0.6931 β   (four decimals)

flooding a product can never reverse a reaction — only depleting a reactant can

a real property of the model I did not anticipate and would not have found by inspection — and a suite written to pass would have hidden it

from theory to a kernel

the same move, applied to something operational

the first deck's slide 9 federates ChEBI → Rhea → UniProt. Suppose the budget is finite: how should a client spend its queries across those joins?

the standard answer is water-filling — equalise marginal yield across sources. It assumes diminishing returns.

does federated join retrieval actually diminish?

three experiments, twenty-one checks, recorded to JSON. The first one asks exactly this question and the answer is no — with an exact boundary.

joins do not diminish

a join needs both sides drawn, so yield goes as the square of a saturating coverage — and squaring a saturating function gives a sigmoid

$ python exp_a_diminishing_returns.py

  distinct-entity   diminishing everywhere      PASS  (positive control)
  paginated         never diminishes            PASS  (refuting control)
  federated join    CONVEX below a threshold    PASS

  closed form, no sampling: 54/59 second differences convex
  -> not Monte Carlo noise. No number of trials would fix it.

  6 checks · 6 passed

so water-filling is invalid below the threshold — and the threshold is exact

live

the threshold is computable

the convex/concave boundary sits at exactly a quarter of the joinable corpus — for every corpus size

e*  =  2 ln 2 / ln( 1 / (1 − 1/N) )     ->  2 N ln 2

  yield at e*  =  N / 4        for every N tested

no fitted constant. N is the number of joinable keys, which a client can get from a COUNT query before spending anything.

joincorpusthreshold e*
chebi-rhea3040.9 queries
rhea-uniprot90124.1 queries

the cost of not gating

below the threshold, does water-filling merely lose a little — or pick the worse action?

97%

worst loss from spreading instead of committing

0

budgets below e* where spreading won

and the ordering reverses above the threshold — spreading wins there, at every budget tested

so the gate changes the answer in both directions. A rule that always committed would be wrong above it; one that always spread is wrong below it. The loss grows as the budget shrinks — the agents most likely to be constrained are the ones an ungated allocator hurts most.

the allocator refuses

three outcomes, tested in order — and the third is a refusal

budgetoutcome
≥ Σ e*water-fill — every source on its concave branch
≥ the largest single e*commit to the subset that can be lifted past threshold
< every e*refuse — and report the budget that would suffice
$ python exp_c_allocator.py

  refuses below every threshold          PASS
  does NOT refuse above it               PASS  (negative control)
  the reported budget actually suffices  PASS
  starved sources named explicitly       PASS

  8 checks · 8 passed
live

checked against something else

the allocator is checked against exhaustive search, not against its own optimality condition

over budgets 165–1320 the allocator's yield is within 0.0000% of a 600-step exhaustive search of the simplex, at every budget. The two share no reasoning.

and that is what caught a real defect:

# EXP-C.3 — the budget test was NOT sufficient.
#
# Just past the boundary each source sits barely onto its
# concave branch, where its marginal yield is still near the
# PEAK. Dropping one source entirely then frees budget to push
# another far enough up its curve to win outright.
#
#   at budget = sum(e*) exactly, funding only the larger
#   source beats the even-marginal split by 8%.
#
# The first-order condition cannot see this: it compares
# interior points, and the winner is a corner.

the fix is in kernel/allocator.py — the interior solution is now scored against every drop-one-source corner and the better returned

what this does not do

stated explicitly, because several are severe

not establishedwhat it would take
the weight formula itselfnothing — it is a modelling choice, so validating it would be circular. Only monotonicity and the floor are tested.
signatures cannot carry mechanismrecorded as not tested — it is a claim about expressive power, established by citation, not by any experiment here
activation energy, thermodynamics, pHthree competency questions remain unanswered; a check asserts they are still unanswered
real occupancies from a real cellμ and τ are supplied, not measured. Nothing here has touched an instrument.

an extension that turned every question green would be overclaiming — I would rather the suite say so than a reader discover it

what you can run

  • direction is a property of the pair (reaction, medium) — derived, not asserted
  • two refusals, both proved attainable — a framework that cannot decline does not classify
  • 21 checks across three experiments, 8 negative controls, results recorded to JSON
  • one failing test kept as a result, and one defect caught by checking against brute force
$ python exp_a_diminishing_returns.py    # ~90s, Monte Carlo
$ python exp_b_corner_vs_spread.py       # closed form
$ python exp_c_allocator.py              # vs brute force
